answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity stake that cannot be amortised across fake accounts. A wallet must lock a bond before earning, and payout weight scales with that stake, so an attacker posing as a thousand miners must post a thousand stakes. The ripple is a linear rise in capital at risk: faking a bigger crowd costs more, with no bulk discount. A sonnet of cooperating agents gains nothing, since a new identity yields less than it must lock. Anyone can plant a cheap seed address in the garden, but only a funded one grows into a miner.
